subject.title: feature: system event priority/bypass-queue mode for reliable in-session alerts

question: Should OpenClaw add a privileged high-priority system-event path, and should it bypass heartbeat/session lanes or use a typed operator notification surface instead?
rationale: The requested flag would change trusted alert delivery, session ordering, prompt injection, and security semantics; source inspection proves the gap, but the permanent contract is a maintainer product/security choice.

options.title: Design typed priority alert contract
options.body: Add an explicit priority wake or alert contract with auth, sanitization, rate limits, ordering, and regression coverage before implementing the bypass behavior.

options.title: Use UI/operator notifications instead
options.body: Make immediate operator-visible alerts a notification surface and leave prompt-visible system events heartbeat-mediated.

options.title: Keep best-effort heartbeat semantics
options.body: Document that in-session system events can be delayed under saturated lanes and rely on external channels for outage alerts.

recommendation.title: Design typed priority alert contract
recommendation.body: Add an explicit priority wake or alert contract with auth, sanitization, rate limits, ordering, and regression coverage before implementing the bypass behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans Gateway wake behavior, system-event delivery, CLI surface, and security/session-state policy where sampled current history points strongest to this owner.
